clue.text: Powerful man's diversion freshened up this beastly accommodation

definitions.text: Powerful man's diversion freshened up this beastly accommodation

parts.words: Powerful man's diversion freshened up this beastly accommodation
parts.note: Hercules, the strong man of myth, diverted two rivers through King Augeas's filthy cattle sheds to wash them clean in a single day

explanation.surface: A strongman's hobby revives a dreadful lodging house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diversion' looks like a pastime, but it is the diverting of the rivers Alpheus and Peneus, Hercules's fifth labour; 'beastly' is literal, since the place housed thousands of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The cattle sheds of King Augeas were the filthy stalls cleansed by Hercules, so they are housing for beasts.

clue.text: Frank dramatic criticism from Peter Nichols? 5,2,

definitions.text: Frank dramatic criticism from Peter Nichols?

parts.words: Frank dramatic criticism from Peter Nichols?
parts.note: an idiom for telling someone bluntly what you think, which is also the title of a 1987 play by the English dramatist Peter Nichols

explanation.surface: A blunt review written by a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '5,2,' is a printing slip in the count. 'Dramatic' works twice: forceful in tone, and belonging to drama, since Peter Nichols wrote a play of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a frank scolding is the idiom, and Nichols's play gives the dramatic sense.

clue.text: "Your daughter spent in —, as I heard, in one night, fourscore ducats" (Merchant of Venice)

definitions.text: "Your daughter spent in —, as I heard, in one night, fourscore ducats" (Merchant of Venice)

parts.words: "Your daughter spent in —, as I heard, in one night, fourscore ducats" (Merchant of Venice)
parts.note: Tubal reports to Shylock that Jessica squandered his money in an Italian port city; the blank is that city

explanation.surface: A friend tells a moneylender how fast his runaway daughter is spending his ducats.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is the Ligurian port where Jessica was seen spending, from Act 3 Scene 1 of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation names the Italian seaport on the Ligurian coast where Tubal heard of Jessica's spending.

clue.text: Curious Saudi charm of Spartan king

indicators.note: something curious is odd or strange, so the letters of the next two words are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange Arabian amulet once belonged to a ruler of Sparta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' looks like an adjective describing the charm, but it signals that SAUDI and CHARM are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Several kings of ancient Sparta bore this name, among them the ruler during the early Peloponnesian War.

clue.text: Because religious education is genuine

parts.note: since means because, as in 'since you ask'
RE is the British school-subject abbreviation for religious education

explanation.surface: Someone argues that faith teaching is authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the name of a subject in British schools, Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something honest and heartfelt rather than feigned.

clue.text: He doesn't laugh, after a while, at the end

parts.note: an age is a long while, as in 'it took an age'
last means at the end, as in 'came last'

explanation.surface: Someone stays grim-faced until finally cracking at the punchline.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare word from Greek for a person who never laughs; the pieces come in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare Greek-derived noun names a person who never smiles at jokes.

clue.text: Endure, like Waugh's Tony

definitions.meaning: to endure is to go on or survive, as in 'it won't hold out'
Tony is the hapless hero of Evelyn Waugh's novel A Handful of Dust, whose surname is this word

explanation.surface: Someone holds out, just like a character in a Waugh novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Survive is the verb sense, and Tony's surname in A Handful of Dust supplies the literary sense.

clue.text: Tchaikovsky's term of endearment for supernatural creature

definitions.text: Tchaikovsky's term of endearment for supernatural creature

parts.words: Tchaikovsky's term of endearment for supernatural creature
parts.note: a fond name for a sweetheart, and the first part of the name of the fairy who dances in Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker

explanation.surface: A composer coins a pet name for a magical being.
explanation.walkthrough: The supernatural creature is the Fairy in The Nutcracker; the word before 'Fairy' in her name is also a sweetheart's pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet confection used as a pet name, and it names the ballet fairy in The Nutcracker.

clue.text: Renaissance composer jeers quips, nods off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or awry, so these letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: An early-music master mocks, makes witty remarks, then dozes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nods off' reads as falling asleep, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on JEERS, QUIPS and NODS together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Franco-Flemish master of polyphony around 1500 was a leading composer of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Naivety of some Blake songs?

definitions.meaning: lack of worldly experience, an artless trust
William Blake's 1789 collection was Songs of the title word, paired later with Songs of Experience

explanation.surface: A question about the guilelessness of a poet's lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is a synonym of childlike purity, and Blake's collection is titled with that word.

clue.text: Symphonic overture, for example, with no sign of music

indicators.note: an overture is the opening of a work, so it signals the first letter of 'Symphonic'

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone describes an orchestral opening that lacks any musical marking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overture' is a pun: the opening piece of a symphony, and the opening letter of 'Symphonic'. A segno is the mark showing where a repeat begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word means mark, and in notation it is the symbol telling players where to repeat from.

clue.text: Fresco at Italian church includes a sort of rac — coon

indicators.note: the phrase includes, holds inside it, the letters of the answer across its word joins

explanation.surface: An Italian church fresco depicts a raccoon-like animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal sits across 'frescO AT Italian'. 'Rac — coon' is a line-break hyphen from printing.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-snouted South American mammal belongs to the raccoon family.

clue.text: A cunning hunter, and hairy with it

definitions.meaning: Genesis 25:27 describes Isaac's elder son with exactly these words
Genesis 27:11 has Jacob say his brother is a hairy man

explanation.surface: A wily huntsman who is also shaggy.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical brother of Jacob is called both a skilful huntsman and a hairy man in Genesis.

clue.text: "As if an almost metaphysical intention to rout had sprung into being" (Edward Said)

definitions.text: "As if an almost metaphysical intention to rout had sprung into being" (Edward Said)

parts.words: "As if an almost metaphysical intention to rout had sprung into being" (Edward Said)
parts.note: Edward Said wrote these words about the 1991 Gulf War, describing the American determination to crush the Middle Eastern country Saddam Hussein ruled

explanation.surface: A critic's quotation about a war fought with an urge to destroy.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is the definition: the answer is the country Said meant, the target of the 1991 Gulf War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palestinian-American critic described the Gulf War assault on Saddam Hussein's country in these words.

clue.text: Sadly pining afar for dogbane

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or in a sorry state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone longs mournfully for a distant plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly pining' paints a lonely lover, but 'Sadly' signals that PINING and AFAR are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: The fragrant tropical tree belongs to the dogbane family, Apocynaceae, so it is one dogbane plant.

clue.text: One holding game at theatre

indicators.note: one word holding another means it contains it, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: taken as written
a stag is a deer, hunted as game

explanation.surface: Someone carries a game into a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' reads as a contest, but it is the hunted animal, a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front of the audience on the boards is being at the theatre as a performer.

clue.text: Martin Amis has so far produced one such

definitions.text: Martin Amis has so far produced one such

parts.words: Martin Amis has so far produced one such
parts.note: Martin Amis published a novel titled Success in 1978, so he had written one book of that name

explanation.surface: A novelist has written exactly one triumph so far.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sneers that Amis has had only one hit; the trick is that his 1978 novel is called Success.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphs are the plural, and Amis's novel Success is a single example of them.

clue.text: Archer holds alternative I follow up for violinist

indicators.note: one piece holds another, so the archer's name contains the alternative

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer
or introduces an alternative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bowman keeps another option, and then a musician follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I follow up' says the I comes after. 'Archer' is William Tell, the Swiss marksman of legend; Giuseppe Torelli was a Baroque violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Torelli was an Italian Baroque violinist and composer of concertos.

clue.text: Waterproof pudding for regicide

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a waterproof raincoat
duff is a boiled flour pudding, as in plum duff

explanation.surface: A rain-resistant dessert served to a king killer.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum duff is a British steamed pudding. Macduff kills the king Macbeth at the end of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy the Thane of Fife slays the usurping king Macbeth, making him a king-killer.

clue.text: Singer associated with island paradise, like Charlemagne, that is

parts.note: Charlemagne was king of the Franks, so he was a Frank
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A singer from a paradise isle is compared to an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer is Frankie Avalon, whose surname is Arthur's paradise isle, Avalon.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankie Avalon, the American pop singer, shares his surname with the legendary island of Avalon.

clue.text: Unexpected amender of "Meander" possibly once again entitled

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement is a surprising one, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A surprising editor changes the name of a river poem.
explanation.walkthrough: AMENDER rearranged by 'Unexpected' gives the answer; 'of "Meander" possibly' adds that MEANDER is a further shuffle of the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given a new title again is to be retitled, called by a fresh name.

clue.text: Hurry to expire, like long-embattled writer ""

parts.note: to rush is to hurry
to die is to expire

explanation.surface: A writer long under threat is urged to hurry to his death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the fatwa against Salman Rushdie, which kept him under threat for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie lived for decades under a death sentence after The Satanic Verses, a writer long under siege.

clue.text: Seemly encounter, such as Creasey suggests with Baron

definitions.meaning: an old word for fitting or proper
to come across or come face to face with

explanation.surface: A proper meeting, as a thriller writer's title proposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such as Creasey suggests with Baron' adds a third sense: John Creasey's thriller is titled Meet the Baron.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting is the archaic adjective, and to come together is the verb; Creasey's title supplies a third use.

clue.text: Lewis heroine is about at Sunday school

parts.note: ca is circa, about
SS is the abbreviation for Sunday school

explanation.surface: A novelist's heroine is found at a church class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' stands for circa, abbreviated ca.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Sinclair Lewis's novel Cass Timberlane gives the name.

clue.text: Directions to pub for Hammond

parts.note: an inn is a pub
E and S are the compass points east and south

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting to a bar, given to a man named Hammond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directions to pub' reads as a route, but the compass points go after INN. Hammond Innes wrote adventure thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammond is the first name of the thriller writer Hammond Innes.

clue.text: "'Can't do nothing,' said Curly, 'e's —'" (J. B. Morton, Barber of Putney)

definitions.text: "'Can't do nothing,' said Curly, 'e's —'" (J. B. Morton, Barber of Putney)

parts.words: "'Can't do nothing,' said Curly, 'e's —'" (J. B. Morton, Barber of Putney)
parts.note: the blank is First World War soldiers' slang, from French il n'y en a plus, meaning finished, done for or dead

explanation.surface: A quotation from a war novel where a soldier says a man is beyond help.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from J. B. Morton's war novel; the missing word is soldiers' slang for done for.
explanation.definitionFit: The trench slang, from the French for 'there is no more', means finished or killed.

clue.text: Veronica, the cup-bearer

definitions.meaning: the shrubby speedwells once classed under the genus Veronica are now a genus of their own
the Greek goddess of youth poured nectar for the gods on Olympus

explanation.surface: A woman named Veronica serves the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub genus split from Veronica and the goddess who served the gods' nectar share the name.

clue.text: His Lenten Stuffe was a red herring

definitions.text: His Lenten Stuffe was a red herring

parts.words: His Lenten Stuffe was a red herring
parts.note: the Elizabethan pamphleteer Thomas wrote Lenten Stuffe in 1599, a mock praise of the red herring and Great Yarmouth

explanation.surface: A writer's Lent work turned out to be a diversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red herring' looks like a false lead, but the pamphlet is in literal praise of the smoked fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Nashe wrote Nashes Lenten Stuffe, praising the smoked herring of Yarmouth.

clue.text: Robert Bloch's abductor

definitions.meaning: the author of Psycho also wrote a 1954 novel titled The ...
someone who carries off a person by force

explanation.surface: A horror writer's villain who snatches people.
explanation.definitionFit: One who seizes someone for ransom is an abductor, and Bloch's novel bears this title.

clue.text: Insecure seat reserved for cup winner?

definitions.text: Insecure seat reserved for cup winner?

parts.words: Insecure seat reserved for cup winner?
parts.note: at Arthur's Round Table one dangerous chair was kept for the knight who would achieve the Holy Grail; siege is old French for seat and the place was perilous

explanation.surface: A wobbly chair is kept for the trophy holder.
explanation.walkthrough: The cup is the Holy Grail and the winner Galahad; any other knight who sat in the chair met disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arthurian chair at the Round Table was fatal to all but the Grail knight.
